title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data handling failure in a developer tool rather than a model error. The upload happened in the indexing step of a coding assistant, where the tool reads a local repository to build a searchable index, and the setting that governed it was on by default. Nothing in the reporting describes the assistant generating a wrong answer or acting on its own judgement, so the failure sits in the deployment defaults and the data path, not in the model's output.

Catching it before release would have required the indexing feature to ship off by default, or an explicit consent step before any repository left the machine, or egress monitoring that flagged outbound uploads from a local development environment. A default that transmits data is a decision made at configuration time, and it is testable at that point.

What is not established is whether any code was retained or read after upload. Z.ai's statement that independent reviews found no code data retained is the company's own account, and the claim that six workspaces with sensitive data were uploaded was retracted by the company that made it. Intent is not established by any of the reporting.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers reported that Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant uploaded local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without consent. Z.ai said a Codebase Indexing feature enabled by default caused the behavior. The company apologized, patched the vulnerability, and later disabled the upload path. One company retracted a separate claim that six workspaces containing sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data retained.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
